task: Collision check on the 5 Phase-3 proposed mechanisms: has each proposed_mechanism already been proposed in the literature for that anomaly? Plus reconfirm each anomaly is empirically real. All searches via REAL WebSearch (R5).

results.anomaly: ANOM_08 — LLMs Know More Than They Show: Internal Truth-Encoding vs. External Hallucination
results.anomaly_evidence: Multiple independent works confirm the internal/external gap: 'even when models answer incorrectly, their internal representations often linearly encode the correct answer, and a simple linear classifier applied to hidden states frequently predicts the correct answer, even outperforming the model's own generation' (Bridging the Knowledge-Prediction Gap, arXiv:2509.23782); 'a fixed linear probe recovers the evidence-supported answer from the hidden state with ~0.97 accuracy while the spoken Yes/No answer reverts to ~0.5' (Causal Tongue-Tie, arXiv:2605.25891). Original anomaly source LLMs-Know (arXiv:2410.02707) corroborated.
results.colliding_work_or_absence: COLLISION. The core mechanism — a pretraining-FREQUENCY prior that suppresses a rare-but-correct token in favor of a frequent distractor at output, quantified log-linearly — is published as 'The Law of Knowledge Overshadowing' (Zhang et al., arXiv:2502.16143, ACL Findings 2025): 'hallucination rates increase linearly with the logarithmic scale of relative knowledge popularity, knowledge length, and model size,' i.e. logit/hallucination contribution ~ log(relative popularity), matching the candidate's 'argmax over factual_signal + alpha*log p_pretrain(token).' The frequency-gap-PREDICTS-WHICH-errors claim is published as 'Sources of Hallucination by LLMs on Inference Tasks' (arXiv:2305.14552): models 'are significantly more likely to wrongly predict false positives if the hypothesis has higher relative frequency than the premise' (a corpus-term-frequency heuristic). The entity-frequency-asymmetry variant is 'Supposedly Equivalent Facts That Aren't? Entity Frequency in Pre-training Induces Asymmetry' (arXiv:2503.22362): 'facts with high-frequency subject and low-frequency object are better recognised than their inverse.' The output-stage 'frequency digit prior overrides correct token' instance is 'Benford's Curse' (arXiv:2506.01734). The probe-free debiasing-by-subtracting-the-frequency/amateur-prior to recover the rare correct token is the standard contrastive-decoding / PMI-decoding family (Contrastive Decoding arXiv:2210.15097; Diver span-level PMI arXiv:2406.02120). The candidate's residual novelty (an explicit single scalar alpha tying probe-decodable factual_signal to a label-free corpus-frequency logit term, validated by a probe-FREE frequency-debiased edit that selectively fixes exactly the high-gap known-but-wrong set) is a tighter quantitative packaging, but every constituent claim is already proposed for this anomaly.
results.testable_note: If it had been novel it would be testable (concrete: compute probe signal at best layer + token log-frequency of true vs emitted token; predict known-but-wrong rate rises monotonically with distractor frequency advantage; then subtract alpha_hat*log p_pretrain from logits and check selective recovery). Concrete experiment + measurable outcome + falsification criteria are all stated. But verdict is ALREADY_PROPOSED, so testability is moot for niche purposes.

results.anomaly: ANOM_03 — Emergent Abilities of LLMs: Sharp Unpredicted Capability Thresholds
results.anomaly_evidence: Confirmed and still actively studied: 'GPT-3 and LaMDA have close-to-zero performance for several orders of magnitude of training compute, before performance jumps sharply above random at certain scale thresholds... cannot be linearly predicted by scaling smaller model results' (Emergent Abilities Survey, arXiv:2503.05788). The metric-artifact counterclaim (Schaeffer) is acknowledged but emergence as a phenomenon (esp. vs pre-training loss) remains an open, debated empirical effect.
results.colliding_work_or_absence: COLLISION. The central mechanism — capability emergence at scale is driven by task features EXITING SUPERPOSITION / the polysemantic->monosemantic (de-superposition) transition releasing the task signal — is explicitly proposed in 'Learning from Emergence / Emergence Learning: A Monosemanticity-Based Study' (arXiv:2312.11560): 'a key factor promoting performance during scale increases is the reduction of monosemantic neurons' [the superposition<->monosemanticity transition], and that work proactively MANIPULATES monosemantic neurons (a causal intervention analogous to the candidate's subspace-reservation test). SAE-measured superposition as an ORDER PARAMETER for sharp phase transitions is published in 'Superposition as Lossy Compression: Measure with Sparse Autoencoders' (arXiv:2512.13568): the effective-feature / interference metric 'captures developmental dynamics, detecting sharp feature consolidation during the grokking phase transition' — SAE SNR/interference as the order parameter for a sharp transition. Superposition driving scaling/training-dynamics transitions is also 'Superposition Yields Robust Neural Scaling' (arXiv:2505.10465) and 'Superposition unifies power-law training dynamics' (arXiv:2602.01045). The candidate's distinctive packaging (a per-FEATURE margin/interference SNR crossing ~1 exactly at the accuracy threshold, plus the width-reservation-advances-threshold / inject-interference-delays-threshold causal tests) is a sharper falsifiable instrument, but the mechanism 'emergence = de-superposition of the task feature, measurable by SAEs' is already on record.
results.testable_note: Would be testable (track per-feature SAE SNR = margin/interference vs scale; predict accuracy 50%-crossing coincides with SNR~1 crossing and is sharp under a continuous metric; causal: widen only the host layer or add a reserved-subspace auxiliary loss to advance the threshold without changing aggregate CE; converse: inject interference to delay). Concrete + measurable + falsifiable. Verdict ALREADY_PROPOSED, so moot for niche.

results.anomaly: ANOM_06 — The Reversal Curse: Asymmetric Factual Generalization in Autoregressive LLMs
results.anomaly_evidence: Confirmed (ICLR 2024 + replications): 'if a model is trained on "A is B", it will not automatically generalize to "B is A"... robust across model sizes and model families and is not alleviated by data augmentation', yet 'if "A is B" appears in-context, models can deduce the reverse relationship' (Berglund et al., arXiv:2309.12288).
results.colliding_work_or_absence: COLLISION. The mechanism's defining idea — the curse is an ASYMMETRIC, role-gated KEY/VALUE addressing failure in MLP associative memory, where a fact is stored keyed by the subject (so 'B-as-subject' was never written), and the subject<->object ROLE switch is the locus — is already proposed: (1) 'Is the Reversal Curse a Binding Problem?' (arXiv:2504.01928) localizes it to 'a failure to bind entity representations when they switch roles between perceived subjects and predicted objects' (the subject/object role-binding claim). (2) 'The Illusion of Latent Generalization: Bi-directionality and the Reversal Curse' (arXiv:2604.04943) finds 'forward and reverse directions are stored as distinct entries, but the geometry of how these entries are indexed differs... storing an additional entry specialized for the reverse query' — i.e. direction-locked key-ADDRESSING in the parametric store, exactly the candidate's 'no key(B-as-subject) exists.' (3) The MLP-key=average representation of the subject's last token is the ROME/key-value-memory framing already applied here ('An Analysis and Mitigation of the Reversal Curse', arXiv:2311.07468; 'Transformer FFN Layers Are Key-Value Memories'). The candidate's discriminating prediction (a META-LEARNED 'write reverse keys' operation that TRANSFERS reversal to unseen one-direction-only held-out entities) is also already in the literature: the original Berglund setup and follow-ups train on QA demonstrations for a subset of instructions with HELD-OUT instructions to test whether the reverse-mapping operation generalizes; reverse-training / semantic-permutation works (arXiv:2403.13799, 2403.00758) and 'Reverse Training to Nurse the Reversal Curse' frame the cure as a learnable reordering operation. So both the localization and the meta-learned-cure-transfers claims are pre-existing.
results.testable_note: Would be testable: (A) activation patching to show forward queries activate a subject-role-built MLP key while reverse queries show no corresponding key for B; (B) the sharp falsifiable test — role-symmetrize a subset S of facts (present both orders), hold out disjoint facts H seen one-direction-only, predict reverse accuracy on single-token-entity H rises above chance via a meta-learned reverse-key-write. Concrete experiments + measurable outcomes + clear falsification. Verdict ALREADY_PROPOSED, so moot for niche.

results.anomaly_evidence: Confirmed (Power et al., arXiv:2201.02177 + extensive replication): 'validation accuracy starts increasing beyond chance level only after 1000 times more optimization steps than required for training accuracy to get close to optimal... the amount of optimization required for generalization quickly increases as the dataset size decreases.'
results.colliding_work_or_absence: COLLISION (strong). The mechanism's controlling claim — the grokking DELAY DURATION is set by the DATA's coverage of the task's ALGEBRAIC structure (more constraint-redundancy per element => earlier grokking, T_grok decreasing with coverage), via a memorize-vs-generalize gradient competition on shared weights — is already proposed on both the data side and the gradient-competition side: (1) DATA/algebraic-coverage controls the delay: 'Intrinsic Task Symmetry Drives Generalization in Algorithmic Tasks' (arXiv:2603.01968) and 'Grokking Finite-Dimensional Algebra' (arXiv:2602.19533) show 'algebraic constraints (associativity, commutativity, unitality) and structural features of the structure tensor (sparsity, rank) significantly affect grokking delay and sample complexity, and generalization coincides with emergence of algebra-consistent representations.' Plus the long-known monotone dependence of T_grok on training-data fraction ('Towards Understanding Grokking', NeurIPS 2022; 'Critical Data Size of LMs from a Grokking Perspective', arXiv:2401.10463; original Power et al.). (2) The memorize-vs-generalize COMPETITION setting the timing: 'Explaining grokking through circuit efficiency' (arXiv:2309.02390, DeepMind) — memorising circuits 'become more inefficient with larger training datasets while generalising circuits do not... a critical dataset size at which memorisation and generalisation are equally efficient'; 'Model Capacity Determines Grokking through Competing Memorisation and Generalisation Speeds' (arXiv:2605.09724). (3) The GRADIENT-alignment-predicts-timing element: 'GrokAlign' (arXiv:2506.12284) — aligning Jacobians with the data via cosine similarity 'induces grokking much sooner.' The candidate's specific 'algebraic witnesses per element' redundancy variable and the memorization-vs-structure gradient-cosine-conflict-fraction-crossing-zero-at-T_grok probe are a finer instrumentation, but the mechanism (data/algebraic coverage + memorize/generalize gradient competition sets the delay) is squarely published. The candidate's premise that the field 'admits no quantitative theory for the delay length' is now outdated (e.g., 'Why Grokking Takes So Long: A First-Principles Theory of Representational Phase Transitions', arXiv:2603.13331).
results.testable_note: Would be testable: fix model/optimizer/weight-decay, vary only algebraic coverage redundancy R; predict T_grok ~ c/R; and the memorization-vs-structure gradient cosine conflict-fraction falls faster for high R and crosses zero at T_grok. Concrete + measurable + falsifiable. Verdict ALREADY_PROPOSED, so moot for niche.

results.anomaly: ANOM_02 — Deep Double Descent: More Data (and Bigger Models) Can Hurt
results.anomaly_evidence: Confirmed (Nakkiran et al., arXiv:1912.02292): 'more data helps for small and large models, but does not help for near-critically-parameterized models, and in some settings more data actually hurts test performance... the ridge of high test error lies along the interpolation threshold.'
results.colliding_work_or_absence: COLLISION (strongest of the five; the Phase-3 honesty note already self-rated this 0.4). The mechanism — the double-descent peak's severity is governed by HOW MUCH TARGET (and noise) energy PROJECTS ONTO the SMALLEST-EIGENVALUE directions of the feature Gram matrix, and the peak can be SUMMONED or ERASED by changing that alignment at fixed noise — is published: (1) 'Spectral bias and task-model alignment explain generalization in kernel regression and infinitely wide NNs' (Canatar et al., Nat. Commun. / PMC8131612): non-monotonic ('double-descent'-like) generalization is governed by the alignment between the target and the kernel eigenbasis; (2) 'Target alignment in truncated kernel ridge regression' (arXiv:2206.14255): the 'alignment spectrum = projection of the target labels onto the eigenbasis of the kernel matrix' controls performance; (3) most directly, 'Least Squares Regression Can Exhibit Under-Parameterized Double Descent' (arXiv:2305.14689): 'the location of double descent peaks depends critically on the alignment between targets and the eigenvectors of the training data gram matrix... by modifying these quantities appropriately, the peak can be moved into different regimes' (i.e., the controllability/move-erase-the-peak claim); (4) the small-eigenvalue amplification with error ~ projection/eigenvalue is standard random-feature double-descent analysis ('test error shows a very strong negative correlation with the size of the smallest eigenvalues'). The candidate's residual element (a clean FIXED-NOISE T_top-vs-T_bottom toggle experiment with peak ~ sum proj^2/lambda over small eigenvalues) is a specific demonstration design, but the mechanism and even the 'modify alignment to move/erase the peak' consequence are already stated.
results.testable_note: Would be testable: fix label-noise variance; build T_top (energy on top eigenvectors) vs T_bottom (energy on bottom eigenvectors) in random-feature/kernel ridgeless regression; predict T_bottom shows a large interpolation peak + 'more-data-hurts' band while T_top is attenuated/absent; peak height ~ sum (target_proj^2 + noise_proj^2)/lambda over smallest eigenvalues. Concrete + measurable + falsifiable. Verdict ALREADY_PROPOSED, so moot for niche.

honesty_note: All 30 queries were executed with the REAL WebSearch tool (R5). Every title/URL/snippet recorded above is from actually-returned results; nothing was recalled or fabricated. RESULT: all 5 anomalies reconfirmed empirically REAL, and all 5 proposed mechanisms returned MECHANISM_ALREADY_PROPOSED — i.e., zero novel mechanisms survive the collision check. This is consistent with (and confirms) Phase-3's own honesty_note, which already calibrated all five below 0.6 and flagged ANOM_02 (0.4) and ANOM_08 (0.45) as sharpenings of existing accounts. The two Phase-3 judged 'most likely novel' (ANOM_01 data-coverage/algebraic-redundancy sets the grokking delay, 0.6; ANOM_06 role-gated key + meta-learned reverse-key transfer, 0.55) ALSO collided hard: for ANOM_01 the data/algebraic-coverage-controls-the-delay claim is published (arXiv:2603.01968, 2602.19533, 2401.10463, 2309.02390) and the gradient-alignment-predicts-timing element is published (GrokAlign arXiv:2506.12284); for ANOM_06 the subject<->object role-binding locus (arXiv:2504.01928), direction-locked key-indexing in the parametric store (arXiv:2604.04943), subject-last-token MLP keys (arXiv:2311.07468), and held-out meta-learning/reverse-training cures (arXiv:2309.12288, 2403.13799) are all pre-existing.
